findings.body:
`identity()` now decodes JWTs with `verify_signature`, `verify_aud`, and `verify_iss` all set to `False`, and no longer passes `SECRET`, `algorithms`, `audience`, or `issuer`. Any client can forge a token with arbitrary claims (user id, roles, tenant) and this function will return them as a trusted identity.

There is no environment check, staging guard, or feature flag around this path — the disable applies wherever `auth.identity` is imported. A temporary re-issuance ticket does not make unsigned tokens safe.

Restore signature verification (and audience/issuer checks) before merge. If staging needs a bridge during migration, use a staging-specific secret/issuer allowlist or a separate explicitly gated decode path — never `verify_signature: False` on the shared identity function.

summary:
## Verdict

**Do not merge.** This change disables JWT signature, audience, and issuer verification unconditionally in `identity()`, which means any caller-supplied token is trusted as identity.

## Why this is blocking

`jwt.decode(..., options={"verify_signature": False, "verify_aud": False, "verify_iss": False})` accepts forged tokens with no shared secret, no `aud`, and no `iss`. There is no staging/env guard, feature flag, or alternate code path — the same function that previously enforced HS256 + audience + issuer now trusts attacker-controlled claims in every environment that runs this module.

The PR description frames this as a temporary staging unblock for token re-issuance (TICKET-412). Temporary intent does not reduce the runtime impact: anyone who can hit an endpoint that calls `identity()` can mint an arbitrary identity dict.

`SECRET` remains in the module but is no longer used by `identity()`, which is consistent with verification being fully removed rather than relaxed in a controlled way.

## Recommendation

Keep verification on. If staging tokens are incompatible after the accounts migration, fix token issuance or accept a staging-only verification key/issuer allowlist — do not disable signature checks on the shared decode path.

**Recommendation:** request-changes
